preconditions.description: The graph has n nodes (1 ≤ n ≤ 500,000) and m edges (m ≥ n - 1, since it is connected).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes within the valid range [1, n].

preconditions.expression: len(set((min(u, v), max(u, v)) for u, v in edges)) == m
preconditions.description: No duplicate edges exist between the same pair of nodes.
The graph is connected and each vertex belongs to at most one simple cycle (implied by the problem statement).

postconditions.expression: len(output) == n and all(1 <= d <= n - 1 for d in output)
postconditions.description: The output is a list of n integers, each representing a valid distance (1 ≤ d ≤ n - 1).

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == max_distance_in_tree(i, edges, removed_edges) for i in range(1, n + 1) for removed_edges in possible_removals(edges))
postconditions.description: For each node i, the output is the minimum possible maximum distance to a leaf in any tree formed by removing edges from the graph.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == min(max(max_distance_to_leaf(i, tree) for tree in possible_trees(edges)) for i in range(1, n + 1)))
postconditions.description: The output for each node i is the smallest maximum distance achievable by optimally removing edges to form a tree.
